content:
maya: heads-up — during last traffic-smoothing rollout the shift stalled at ~70% and autopilot auto-reverted. suspect some backend affinity / probe mismatch + node placement failures. logs show a bunch of `503` + `upstream reset` around the cutoff window.
liam: ugh. which release and cluster?
maya: prod-eu-west1, release v2.14.3, splitter operator kicked off the smoothing window at 00:12 UTC. deploy-bot: canary shift started -> 10% -> 40% -> 70% -> paused -> rollback triggered by latency spike.
raj: we had a terraform apply earlier that rebuilt the gpu-nodepool with new labels. possible drift: autoscaler rule expects `nodepool: inference-v2` but nodes came up as `nodepool: inference-v2a`.
sofia: @raj can you paste the drift diff?
raj: short snippet from `terraform plan` I saw: `- label "nodepool=inference-v2" + label "nodepool=inference-v2a"`. autoscaler matcher in helm values is `selector: nodepool=inference-v2`.
helena: also saw readiness/ liveness mismatch on the new pods — readinessProbe initialDelay 1s, TTL 10s on the service side, so connection tracking could keep previous backends sticky. if sticky sessions are on, traffic keeps hitting old pods that are terminating.
maya: sample svc dump:
```
$ kubectl describe svc inference-svc -n prod
Name: inference-svc
Type: ClusterIP
Session Affinity: ClientIP
Endpoints: 10.12.5.8:8080, 10.24.3.6:8080 (some are old IPs)
```
liam: SessionAffinity ClientIP + kube-proxy conntrack + fast termination = classic affinity leak. we should avoid ClientIP for canary services or use a stable proxy (envoy) with drain timeout.
sofia: deploy-bot posted: `rollout: paused (latency spike), auto-revert in 30s` — we need to stop auto-revert until we validate autoscaler/labels.
raj: i can open a quick terraform rollback to old labels but that won't fix long-term. prefer patching helm chart to support both selectors or use nodeAffinity instead of label string.
helena: quick mitigation: set service.sessionAffinity: None for the canary split and bump graceful termination to 60s. also increase readinessProbe initialDelay to 10s for new nodes so they don't join traffic too early.
maya: agreed. also note eu-west1 had spot GPU allocation pressure around that window — a few pods ended up Pending before landing in other AZ, which confused the splitter weight calc.
liam: can we patch the progressive delivery operator to account for Pending pods when computing target weights? it should only count Ready endpoints.
sofia: created ticket INF-4382 linking drift + probe + capacity: https://redwood.example.com/INF-4382
maya: action items:
- raj: create terraform PR to align labels + fallback matcher (in 30m)
- liam: patch helm preStop hook and increase terminationGracePeriod (will PR)
- helena: change svc sessionAffinity to None for canary route + bump probes (will do canary patch)
- sofia: pause auto-revert window until we've validated fixes (ops console)
- maya: follow up on GPU capacity report with cloud vendor (booking requests)

liam: small snippet for patch to values.yaml:
```yaml
service:
  sessionAffinity: None
pod:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
  readinessProbe:
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
```
raj: copying that into the terraform/helm sync PR. will reference INF-4382.
deploy-bot: redeploy scheduled: canary-patch-174990 -> queued by sofia
maya: thanks team — will monitor next rollout and report back. :eyes:
